desc:
Treat the binary tree as an undirected graph: you may walk from a node to its parent as well as to its children, and each step along an edge costs 1.

For every node, find the largest distance (in edges) from that node to any node of the tree. Return these values as an array in level-order of the real nodes, that is, in the same order in which the real (non--1) entries appear in the input. The empty tree gives [].

How trees are given. There is no tree type here. A binary tree is passed as an integer array in level-order (top to bottom, left to right), the same way LeetCode serialises trees. A missing child is written as -1, and every real node value is non-negative. The children of a missing node are not listed, and trailing -1 entries are dropped, so a non-empty array never ends with -1. The empty tree is [].

For example, [1, 2, 3, -1, 4] describes the tree on the left: the root is 1 with children 2 and 3, node 2 has no left child and has 4 as its right child, and node 3 is a leaf.

    1
   / \
  2   3
   \
    4

For tree = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] the nodes in order are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and the answer is [2, 2, 3, 3, 3]: for example node 1 reaches node 4 in 2 steps, while node 4 needs 3 steps to reach node 3.
constraints: The array follows the encoding above exactly (valid level-order, no trailing -1)
hints: Running a breadth-first search from every node works, but it costs O(n<sup>2</sup>) in total, which is needless for a tree.
Think about the diameter. For any node, one of the two end points of a longest path in the tree is always a farthest node from it.

Find the two diameter end points a and b with BFS (BFS from any node to the farthest node a, then BFS from a to the farthest node b). The answer for a node is max(dist(node, a), dist(node, b)), so one more BFS from b finishes the job.
editorial: A classic fact about trees: a farthest node from any node can be chosen among the two ends a, b of a diameter. So after finding a diameter, each node's eccentricity is the maximum of its distance to a and its distance to b.

To find the diameter ends: BFS from any node (say the root) and take the farthest node as a; BFS from a and take the farthest node b. A third BFS from b gives the second set of distances. Three BFS passes over the n-1 edges give O(n) total time.

The undirected adjacency list is built from the level-order array: the k-th real node has its children at slots 2k+1 and 2k+2. Special cases: the empty tree gives an empty array, and a single node gives [0].
